prompt: Hey, need to decide on warehouse automation vendors for the board meeting Thursday. We've got two quotes. Vendor A is $2.4M upfront, 12-month rollout. Vendor B is $3.1M, 9-month rollout, and they claim 15% higher throughput. Our peak season is in 10 months, so timing matters. I'm leaning A honestly because the lower upfront cost is easier to justify to the CFO, but the faster rollout for B could help us handle the holiday rush better. What do you think? Also, I haven't factored in ongoing maintenance costs yet, which might change things. The reader is our CFO, Maria, and she needs to pick one to present to the board. She'll want to know the trade-offs clearly. Can you draft something for her?

We need to decide on the tip-allocation feature for our payroll software. Building it in-house will cost about $180K and take 4 months. Or we can license an existing solution for $95K per year, and it'd be integrated in about a month. I'm not sure which way to go. The in-house option gives us more control and we could customize it later, but the licensing is faster and cheaper upfront. The VP of Product, David, needs to make the call. He'll want to see the cost comparison, the timeline difference, and the long-term implications. We also haven't figured out how much maintenance the licensed option would require from our team. Can you put together a clear message for him?

Quick one. We're deciding on the ad campaign for next quarter. We have $50K to spend. Option A is a Google Ads campaign, projected CAC is $18 per patient. Option B is a Facebook campaign, projected CAC is $22 per patient. We could also split the budget. I'm leaning Facebook actually because our audience is really active there, even if the CAC is higher. The Head of Growth, Sarah, needs to decide. She'll want to know the expected number of patients we can get with each option and the total cost. Also, we haven't accounted for the lifetime value of a patient, which might make a higher CAC worthwhile. Can you write this up for her?

We're trying to hit the $2M ARR target this year. We're 40 people now. I'm looking at hiring. Option 1: two sales reps at $160K base each. Option 2: one enterprise rep at $210K. The enterprise rep would focus on larger accounts, but the two reps could cover more ground. I have no strong preference yet. The COO, Alex, needs to decide on the hiring plan. He'll want to see the total cost, the expected coverage, and how each option aligns with our sales strategy. We also don't know the typical ramp-up time for each type of hire. Can you draft a message for him to make this decision?

Weekly update on the backend migration. We moved the user-auth service over to the new system, that's done. We're blocked on the payment-service migration because we need an answer from the DBA about the database schema change. The code-freeze date is still not confirmed, we're waiting on the release manager. The Director of Engineering, Ravi, needs this update. No decision needed from him right now, just want to keep him in the loop. Also, we noticed a small issue with the logging in the new system, but it's not blocking anything. Let me know if you need more details. Can you write the status update?

Monthly update on the subscription transition. So far, 60% of our contracts have been converted to annual billing. One contract is still in legal review, that's with the Northwind account. We're also validating the revenue recognition model for the new 'sensor-as-a-service' tier. The VP of Finance, Priya, needs this update. She doesn't need to make a decision now, just wants the status. We also saw a slight uptick in support tickets related to the new billing, but it's manageable. Let me know if there's anything else you need. Can you draft the update for me?

Daily tracker update on the tutor-payout system. We've processed payouts for 80% of tutors. One bank-integration API is down, which is blocking the remaining 20%. The next payout run is uncertain until that's fixed. The Head of Operations, Maria, needs this update. No decision required, just a heads-up. We're monitoring the situation and will provide more info when the API is back. Also, we had a question about a specific tutor's payout, but that's a separate issue. Can you write this up?

Here's the diff summary for the retry-logic fix in the payment webhook. Changed 3 files, added 45 new tests, and 3 of those are new tests for the retry scenarios. All 45 tests are passing. One thing we haven't tested is the out-of-order event delivery case. The reviewer, Jane, needs to look at this and approve the merge. She'll want to understand the changes and the test coverage. Also, we noticed a potential race condition but it's not in the scope of this fix. Can you write a PR description for me?

PR description for the caching layer in the session-store service. The diff shows we reduced latency from 120ms to 30ms. Changed 5 files, added a new cache manager. The reviewer, David, needs to review and sign off. He'll want to know the performance improvement and the implementation details. We haven't tested the cache-eviction race condition yet, so that's a known gap. Also, we have a few edge cases with cache invalidation that we're still thinking through. Can you draft the PR description?

Here's the full customer-churn analysis. We looked at churn rates by segment, the revenue impact, and proposed retention actions. Segment A has a churn rate of 5% and contributes $200K in monthly revenue. Segment B has a churn rate of 8% and contributes $150K. Segment C has a churn rate of 12% and contributes $100K. The proposed actions include a loyalty program for Segment A, a personalized onboarding for Segment B, and a win-back campaign for Segment C. I'm leaning towards prioritizing Segment B because the revenue impact is significant and the churn rate is moderate. But I'm open to other interpretations. The CEO, Sarah, needs to decide which segment to prioritize. She'll want a clear executive summary with the key numbers and the rationale for each option. Can you write this for her?
